column1: # fails the build if a guard script exists but is not registered, so a new guard
#   guard      path to the guard script, relative to the repo root
#   class      the pattern class it owns
#              gating   = a non-zero exit fails a mandatory build path
#              advisory = informational; it does not stop a merge
#              yes = `validate-guards.sh` runs it (in the ci.yml `audit` job)
#              no  = it gates elsewhere (noted) or is advisory
#   owner      the team accountable for the class
#   notes      how it gates / what it does

column6: notes
meta: registry integrity; runs the gating set below
new production panic is removed or baselined (ratchet)
new production unsafe is removed or baselined (ratchet)
tracing a secret-ish identifier must be redacted
a `(( X++ ))` under errexit ends the script on bash 4.4+ (and silently, before any verdict); gates via its own `Shell exit status` CI stage, and scans every copy of the mirrored scripts (#1291)
mirrored .pi/scripts must be byte-identical across trees unless recorded (with a reason) in .pi/script-drift-allow.tsv

every relative doc link must resolve; CHANGELOG.md's newest version must equal engine/Cargo.toml's; every backticked identifier in a README must exist in the source — a doc may not point at a removed file, drift behind the tags, or name a type that is not in the code
claims that a control is wired, re-resolved against the code (both directions: evidence gone, or a GAP silently restored)

ADR-014's exclusion counts are recomputed from engine/.pi/portable-inventory.tsv's rows and compared with the summary, the module list and ADR-014 — a summary that disagrees with its own rows, or a record that states a different ratio, fails (#1361)

the per-layer coverage floors may not be lowered: every layer's floor in .pi/coverage-layers.tsv is compared with the base commit and fails naming the layer, the old value and the new one when it falls — or when a layer loses its row; gates in the `coverage` job, which needs the base ref (2 commits of history), so it is not in this job's set (#1427)
gates via the CI lint+build+test jobs; aggregate fmt/clippy/test/audit
gates via the CI test job and conformance

cargo audit + ad-hoc secret scan; WARN-only. Installed in all 5 trees; resolves its crate(s) from its OWN path, so it is cwd-independent (tree root = every crate). Advisory because its heuristics are noisy — the real dependency audit + secret scan gate in the CI audit job
module-layering heuristic
release-readiness heuristic
@canonical reference check
glossary drift check
production-readiness heuristic
integration heuristic
the 150-check effect-commitment contract proof runs here with a real exit code; --self-test seeds a removed contract and requires a failure (#1186)
the capacity-ledger contract proof runs here with a real exit code; --self-test seeds a removed contract and requires a failure (#1186)
cargo check --workspace --all-targets; catches a public-enum addition breaking a downstream exhaustive match (#1195)
audit-ignore expiry and docs/issues front-matter vocabulary; --self-test seeds both violations (#1203)
an intra-workspace path-dep pin equals the crate it points at

the train is derived from `cargo metadata`, not from release.yml's literal: every publishable member (publish != false) must be named in the version loop, have a `publish-crate.sh` step, carry the train version, appear in the release notes, and — for the host-facing npm package — be wired in or out of `github-release.needs` according to `wasm/ci/bundle-budget.txt`'s readiness state; `--self-test` seeds 13 defects (#1346, #1434)
